interactions.summary: Students offer pro-immigration arguments about labor supply and global unity; Jiang concedes their force while exposing the exploitative and symbolic tradeoffs inside them.

claims.claim: A student says developed economies often rely on immigrant workers as a cheaper labor source.
Jiang replies that this amounts to importing poor people in order to exploit them, which exposes the moral ugliness of the cheap-labor defense.
Another student argues that widespread cultural mixing can create world unity by placing every culture inside every country.
Jiang accepts the unity image and uses the World Cup in America as an example of multicultural celebration.

signature_moments.moment: The labor-market defense of immigration is exposed as a plan to exploit the poor more cheaply.
signature_moments.source_phrase: bring in poor people to exploit
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It captures Jiang's habit of forcing a respectable economic rationale to state its hidden moral premise out loud.

chronology_notes.note: The class now actively mounts the strongest arguments against Jiang's anti-immigration reading, especially labor utility and multicultural unity.
